claim: The style began in Victoria's Great Western and survives almost nowhere else on earth.
because: The Shiraz-based sparkling red style is usually credited to Edmond Mazure at Auldana, near Adelaide in South Australia, around 1894-95, and he is the pioneer candidates are taught. Great Western in Victoria was a parallel pioneer: Hans Irvine made a sparkling red there from Pinot in the early 1890s, and Seppelt moved it to Shiraz later. An earlier pink 'sparkling burgundy' came from the Victorian Champagne Company in Melbourne. So it is false to say the style began at Great Western.
fix: The style took shape in the 1890s, when Edmond Mazure at Auldana in South Australia and Hans Irvine at Great Western in Victoria both made sparkling reds, and it survives almost nowhere else on earth.
